answer: Because the prism cliff is fixed at deposit and recorded in the lagoon ledger, the lotus audit exposes how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 24 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. A farm of 175 pays that 63 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
